speaker: lead
text: Okay, shall we start? Haeun's previous meeting is running long, so Haeun will be about five minutes late.

speaker: member_a
text: Sure. Oh, would you like some coffee? I heard the coffee machine in the break room got fixed this morning.

speaker: lead
text: Really? It was broken all last week, so I went all the way down to the café downstairs.

speaker: member_b
text: Me too. Buying it every day, the coffee alone adds up to quite a bit each month.

speaker: member_a
text: They say the new beans are a bit nuttier. I tried it earlier and it was pretty good. It's less acidic, which I actually like.

speaker: member_b
text: I prefer a bit of acidity. But it's free, so I'll drink it anyway.

speaker: lead
text: Did everyone have a good weekend? Emily, weren't you moving?

speaker: member_a
text: Yes, I moved on Saturday. I had more stuff than I thought, so I haven't even unpacked half the boxes yet.

speaker: member_b
text: I feel like it takes a month to settle in after a move. When I moved last year, I didn't unpack the kitchen boxes for two months.

speaker: member_a
text: Still, I'm thirty minutes closer to the office now, so my mornings are way more relaxed.

speaker: lead
text: That's huge. A shorter commute is the best.

speaker: lead
text: I'll have to go grab a cup later. Okay, let's get down to business. Today's meeting is to prepare next quarter's team workshop.

speaker: lead
text: The most urgent thing is the date. Once that's set we can move on the rest, so let's start with the date.

speaker: member_a
text: I checked the team calendar, and the second and third Fridays of November are more or less free.

speaker: member_b
text: On the second Friday I have a client visit scheduled. It's not confirmed yet, but I'll probably go.

speaker: lead
text: Can't that visit be moved?

speaker: member_b
text: It's on the client's schedule, so it's hard for me to move it. Their contact person is only in Korea that week.

speaker: member_a
text: The third Friday is the 21st, and everyone else on the team seems to be free that day.

speaker: lead
text: What about the fourth week? I'm a bit nervous having only one option.

speaker: member_a
text: The fourth week is month-end, so everyone is busy with closing. Last year we did it at month-end and half the people brought their laptops.

speaker: lead
text: Oh, that's right. Let's avoid that.

speaker: member_c
text: Sorry I'm late. My previous meeting ran longer than expected. What were you talking about?

speaker: lead
text: The workshop date. The third Friday, the 21st, came up. Haeun, are you free that day?

speaker: member_c
text: One moment, let me check my calendar. Yes, the 21st is open.

speaker: lead
text: So Friday, November 21st works for everyone, right?

speaker: member_a
text: Yes, sounds good.

speaker: member_b
text: That day works for me too.

speaker: member_c
text: Me too.

speaker: lead
text: Great, the date is confirmed: Friday, November 21st.

speaker: member_b
text: So what kind of budget are you thinking? I feel like we'd need at least 100,000 won per person this time to do anything.

speaker: lead
text: 100,000 won? Last year it was 50,000 won per person.

speaker: member_a
text: With 50,000 won, there's almost nothing left after lunch. That's why we didn't have much to do in the afternoon last year either.

speaker: member_b
text: Exactly. So this time I'd like us to ask for more. I hear other companies spend a lot more on team workshops.

speaker: member_c
text: But this year the whole company is cutting back, so I don't think it'll be easy. I heard other teams scaled down their events too.

speaker: member_a
text: I heard the sales team isn't doing a workshop at all this time.

speaker: lead
text: Not at all? That team is huge, too.

speaker: member_a
text: They switched to one big dinner at the end of the year instead.

speaker: member_b
text: But we beat our targets last year. Couldn't we at least bring that up?

speaker: member_c
text: If we're going to make that case, we should put some numbers together. I have last year's performance data.

speaker: member_b
text: If 100,000 won is hard, even 80,000 won would be nice.

speaker: member_a
text: I think even around 70,000 won would be fine for me.

speaker: lead
text: I'll have to ask the director about that first. We can't decide on an amount here right now.

speaker: member_b
text: Okay, please let us know once you've checked.

speaker: lead
text: Sure, I'll ask this week.

speaker: member_a
text: Oh, and did you hear the quarterly report deadline got moved up to next Wednesday?

speaker: lead
text: What? Wasn't it originally Friday?

speaker: member_a
text: The planning team sent an email yesterday. The executive meeting got scheduled for Thursday, so they want it a day before.

speaker: lead
text: Oh, I haven't seen that email yet. If it's moved up two whole days, that's tight.

speaker: member_b
text: Then we need to pull all the numbers this week. I still haven't finished filling in the Q3 sales table.

speaker: member_c
text: I still have to organize the customer survey results too. The responses came in later than expected.

speaker: lead
text: How many survey responses do we have?

speaker: member_c
text: A little over two hundred right now. The goal was three hundred, but if we close it this Friday, we'll have about two hundred fifty.

speaker: lead
text: Two hundred fifty is enough for the analysis. Let's just close it on Friday.

speaker: member_c
text: Okay, I'll close it at six on Friday and put it into tables over the weekend.

speaker: lead
text: Take the weekend off. Monday is fine.

speaker: member_b
text: For the sales table, I need the final numbers from finance, and they say that'll be Monday.

speaker: member_a
text: If finance is late, how about putting in preliminary numbers first like last year and swapping them later?

speaker: member_b
text: That's an option, but last year the preliminary and final numbers were pretty different, and it caused trouble.

speaker: member_c
text: Right, at the executive meeting we got a ton of questions about why the numbers changed.

speaker: member_b
text: Exactly. Since then I only put in final numbers.

speaker: lead
text: I get that. Since the schedule is tight this time, I'll ask finance to send them by Monday morning.

speaker: member_b
text: That would really help.

speaker: lead
text: Then we put them in as soon as we get them Monday, and go over it together on Tuesday. And submit Wednesday morning.

speaker: member_a
text: Does three o'clock Tuesday afternoon work? I'll book a meeting room.

speaker: lead
text: Yes, that's fine. Emily, could you take care of merging the drafts?

speaker: member_a
text: Sure, I'll do it. Everyone just upload your parts to the shared folder by Monday evening.

speaker: member_c
text: We can use last quarter's template as is, right?

speaker: member_a
text: Yes, same template, but this time they want a one-page summary at the very front.

speaker: lead
text: I'll write the summary. Everyone, just send me your top three numbers separately.

speaker: member_c
text: Oh, and by the way, where did they decide to seat the new intern? The intern is still at that empty desk by the window.

speaker: lead
text: When the seating changes next week, the intern is moving over to our team's area.

speaker: member_b
text: Good. Right now the intern sits a bit far away, so it's awkward to ask anything.

speaker: member_c
text: Are the intern's laptop and accounts set up?

speaker: lead
text: The laptop is ready, but a few internal system permissions still haven't come through. I'll talk to IT about it again.

speaker: member_b
text: Permission requests go faster with the department head's approval. You'll probably need to click approve.

speaker: lead
text: Oh, really? Then I'll check right after the meeting.

speaker: member_a
text: Then maybe around next Monday we could have lunch together and say hi.

speaker: member_c
text: Sounds good. I'll ask the intern what they like to eat.

speaker: member_b
text: Last time the intern mentioned liking spicy food. How about that malatang place?

speaker: member_a
text: Malatang sounds great. Let's go there for lunch on Monday.

speaker: lead
text: Good. I'll send a separate note about that.

speaker: member_c
text: So what should we do about the workshop venue?

speaker: lead
text: Let's look at the venue at the next meeting, after the headcount and how much we can spend are settled. It feels a bit early right now.

speaker: member_c
text: Okay, got it.

speaker: lead
text: Look at the time already. Let's stop here for today and pick up the rest at the next meeting.

speaker: member_a
text: When should we schedule the next meeting?

speaker: lead
text: How about next Thursday afternoon? The report will be done by then, so we'll have a bit more room.

speaker: member_b
text: Thursday afternoon works for me.

speaker: member_c
text: Works for me too.

speaker: lead
text: Then I'll send an invite for next Thursday at two. Good work, everyone.
